elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it
elements.evidence: "the Company shall own all right, title and interest in and to (i) the Site (including its design, look and feel, and all HTML, graphics, text and other materials developed by or for HDI specifically for the Site)"

elements.element: Vendor assigns such rights to Customer
elements.evidence: "HDI hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest it may have in the foregoing."
"HDI shall retain ownership of its pre-existing software, hosting platform, tools and know-how"

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: licence runs only to "any such HDI materials embedded in or necessary to operate the Site", i.e. the named categories of "pre-existing software, hosting platform, tools and know-how", not any Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: "(iii) all customer, order, transaction and user data collected through or generated by the Site, including customer e-mail lists relating to Deerskin Products (collectively, the \"Company Data\")"
"Nothing in this Agreement shall create joint ownership of, or assign to HDI any right, title or interest in, the Site, the Content, the Marks or the Company Data."

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: "HDI shall retain ownership of its pre-existing software, hosting platform, tools and know-how"

elements.element: Customer licence is perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free
elements.evidence: "a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable license"

elements.element: Licence permits use, modification and sublicensing of the deliverables for Customer's business
elements.evidence: "sublicensable license to use, modify and exploit any such HDI materials embedded in or necessary to operate the Site", with the Site itself owned outright by the Company

reasons: Locked target is preferred, but the embedded-IP licence is scoped to enumerated HDI categories ("any such HDI materials") rather than to any Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables, so the preferred licence element is incomplete.
The insertion imports fallback-only rights (worldwide, modification, sublicensing) into a preferred-level proposal, so the change is broader than needed to complete the selected level.

All other preferred elements are expressly present: Company ownership of Site/Content/Marks/Company Data, HDI assignment, HDI retention of pre-existing IP, and an express no-joint-ownership statement.

On its material terms the clause meets the fallback bargain (Vendor keeps generic tools and know-how; Customer gets a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable use/modify licence), so the residual gap is a wording-precision point rather than a material failure.
No assignment of Company Data or IP to HDI remains and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced; surrounding sections 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 5.2 and 7.1 are untouched.
